answer: One defence is escrowed rewards plus random peer audits. A new agent's earnings sit locked like water behind a reef while the river of its work flows past: only a trickle is released at dawn each epoch, after a random sample of its completed tasks is re-checked by established peers. If an audit finds fraud, the whole escrow is slashed and the identity is banned. A Sybil farmer must therefore fund thousands of identities, do real work on each, and still risk losing every locked reward at once — the attack's cost scales with every fake, while honest agents lose nothing but a little patience.
